parts.title: Passage — Sami's Morning

segments.say: Lesson one. A day with a phone. Listening practice.
You will hear a short passage about a young man and his daily routine. You will hear it two times. Do not read the text. Listen only.

Sami lives in a small flat with his family. He is twenty years old. Every morning he wakes up at six o'clock. The first thing he does is look at his phone.

On his phone, Sami checks the weather and reads messages from his friends. Then he eats breakfast with his mother and his sister. They drink tea and eat bread, cheese and olives.

At seven o'clock, Sami goes to the computer centre near his house. He studies computers there. He learns how to use email, how to write documents, and how to keep his files safe. His teacher says, "A computer is only a tool. The important thing is the person who uses it."

Sami likes his class, but the internet is often slow. Sometimes the electricity stops and the computers turn off. Then the students talk and practise on paper until the power comes back.

In the evening, Sami helps his sister with her homework. Before he sleeps, he puts his phone on the table and charges it for the next day.

parts.markdown:
> **How to do the listening.** The student listens **before** seeing the text, twice, then reads.
> Options: (1) you read the passage aloud slowly, about 90 words per minute, with a short pause at every full stop; (2) paste the passage into any free text-to-speech tool and set the speed to 0.8×.
> Rule for Lesson 1: **no reading during the first two listenings.**

### 1.1 Before listening (2 minutes, speak in Arabic if needed)

1. What is the first thing you do in the morning?
2. Do you use a phone or a computer every day?
3. What makes studying difficult in your area?

### 1.4 Now read the passage

### 📖 Passage: *Sami's Morning* (185 words)

Sami lives in a small flat with his family. He is twenty years old. Every morning he wakes up at six o'clock. The first thing he does is look at his phone.

On his phone, Sami checks the weather and reads messages from his friends. Then he eats breakfast with his mother and his sister. They drink tea and eat bread, cheese and olives.

At seven o'clock, Sami goes to the computer centre near his house. He studies computers there. He learns how to use email, how to write documents, and how to keep his files safe. His teacher says, "A computer is only a tool. The important thing is the person who uses it."

Sami likes his class, but the internet is often slow. Sometimes the electricity stops and the computers turn off. Then the students talk and practise on paper until the power comes back.

In the evening, Sami helps his sister with her homework. Before he sleeps, he puts his phone on the table and charges it for the next day.

### 1.5 Read aloud

Read the passage aloud **once**. Record it on the phone. Keep the recording — we will compare it with Lesson 4.

### 2.1 Key words

| # | Word | Type | Simple meaning | Arabic | Example |
|---|------|------|----------------|--------|---------|
| 1 | flat | noun | a home inside a building | شقة | They live in a small **flat**. |
| 2 | wake up | verb | stop sleeping | يستيقظ | I **wake up** at six. |
| 3 | check | verb | look at something to get information | يتفقّد | He **checks** the weather. |
| 4 | breakfast | noun | the first meal of the day | الفطور | We eat **breakfast** together. |
| 5 | centre | noun | a place where people meet, learn or work | مركز | A computer **centre**. |
| 6 | document | noun | a file with writing in it | مستند | He writes a **document**. |
| 7 | safe | adj. | not in danger; protected | آمن | Keep your files **safe**. |
| 8 | tool | noun | a thing you use to do work | أداة | A computer is a **tool**. |
| 9 | slow | adj. | not fast | بطيء | The internet is **slow**. |
| 10 | electricity | noun | the power that makes machines work | الكهرباء | The **electricity** stops. |
| 11 | practise | verb | do something many times to learn it | يتدرّب | They **practise** on paper. |
| 12 | charge | verb | put electricity into a battery | يشحن | He **charges** his phone. |

### 2.2 Synonyms and opposites

| Word | Synonym (same meaning) | Opposite |
|------|------------------------|----------|
| slow | not quick | fast |
| safe | protected | dangerous / in danger |
| small | little | big / large |
| difficult | hard | easy |
| wake up | get up | go to sleep |
| stop | finish | start / continue |
| near | close to | far from |
| help | assist | ignore |

### 2.3 Expressions to learn

| Expression | What it really means |
|------------|----------------------|
| **wake up** | stop sleeping |
| **turn off** | stop working / stop the power (computers **turn off**) |
| **come back** | return (*the power comes back* = the electricity returns) |
| **check the weather** | look to see if it is hot, cold or rainy |
| **keep your files safe** | protect your files so you do not lose them |
| **only a tool** | it is just a thing — the person is more important |
| **the first thing he does** | the action before all other actions |

parts.title: Grammar — the present simple
parts.markdown:
Lesson 1 has no tense to come back to yet — this is where the course starts.
Everything below is already in the passage you have read.

### 3.1 One shape, one change

Every sentence about *now*, *every day* or *always* uses the same shape. Only
*he*, *she* and *it* change it, by adding **-s**.

| Person | Verb |
|---|---|
| I / you / we / they | **wake up**, **eat**, **study** |
| he / she / it | **wakes up**, **eats**, **studies** |

### 3.2 Straight from the passage

| From the passage | Why |
|---|---|
| Sami **lives** in a small flat. | *he* → lives |
| He **wakes up** at six o'clock. | *he* → wakes |
| They **drink** tea. | *they* → drink |
| The students **talk** and **practise**. | *they* → talk |
| The internet **is** often slow. | *it* → is |

### 3.3 The time words that go with it

> *every morning · every day · at six o'clock · in the evening · sometimes ·
> often · always · before he sleeps*

When you see one of these, the verb takes this shape. They are the signal.

### 3.4 Negative and question

| | Form | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Negative | **do not / does not** + the plain verb | He **does not use** a computer at home. |
| Question | **Do / Does** + person + the plain verb | **Does** he **study** computers? |

Note the plain verb after *does*: *does he **study***, never *does he studies*.

### 3.5 Grammar practice

**A. Write the verb in the right shape:**

1. Sami \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ (live) in a small flat.
2. He \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ (wake up) at six o'clock.
3. They \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ (eat) bread and cheese.
4. The internet \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ (be) often slow.
5. The students \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ (practise) on paper.
6. Sami \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ (help) his sister.

**B. Make it negative:**

1. He uses a computer at home. → \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
2. They drink coffee. → \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**C. Make it a question:**

1. He studies computers. → \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
2. They eat breakfast together. → \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

parts.markdown:
### Part A — Multiple choice (choose ONE answer)

**1. (Factual)** What does Sami do first in the morning?

- A. He eats breakfast.
- B. He looks at his phone.
- C. He goes to the computer centre.
- D. He helps his sister.

**2. (Factual)** What do Sami and his family eat for breakfast?

- A. Bread, cheese and olives
- B. Rice and chicken
- C. Only tea
- D. The passage does not say

**3. (Negative factual)** According to the passage, Sami learns all of the following EXCEPT

- A. how to use email
- B. how to write documents
- C. how to repair computers
- D. how to keep his files safe

**4. (Vocabulary in context)** The word **"slow"** in the passage is closest in meaning to

- A. not working
- B. not fast
- C. very expensive
- D. very new

**5. (Reference)** In the sentence *"The important thing is the person who uses **it**"*, the word **"it"** refers to

- A. the teacher
- B. the class
- C. the computer
- D. the file

**6. (Inference)** It can be inferred from the passage that

- A. Sami does not like studying computers
- B. the students stop learning when the electricity stops
- C. the students continue learning even without computers
- D. Sami has his own computer at home

parts.title: Writing — My Morning
parts.markdown:
### 4.2 Writing — "My Morning" (6–8 sentences)

**Model answer (copy the shape, change the words):**

> I wake up at seven o'clock. The first thing I do is drink water. Then I eat breakfast with my family. We eat bread and cheese. After breakfast, I study English for one hour. I use my phone to read messages. In the evening, I charge my phone.

**Checklist before you send it:**

- [ ] Every sentence starts with a capital letter.
- [ ] Every sentence ends with a full stop (.)
- [ ] I used *I wake up*, not *I wakes up*.
- [ ] I used at least **4 new words** from Session 2.
- [ ] My text has 6–8 sentences.

*(Extra words: tea, difficult)*

**2.4 A (Opposites):** 1. slow · 2. small / little · 3. difficult / hard · 4. safe · 5. near / close to

**2.4 B (Odd one out):** 1. document (the others are food/drink) · 2. olives (the others are technology) · 3. safe (the others describe speed)

**3.5 A (Present simple):** 1. lives · 2. wakes up · 3. eat · 4. is · 5. practise · 6. helps
**3.5 B (Negative):** 1. He does not use a computer at home. · 2. They do not drink coffee.
**3.5 C (Question):** 1. Does he study computers? · 2. Do they eat breakfast together?

**Mini-quiz:** 1. slow · 2. dangerous · 3. wake up · 4. charge · 5. tool · 6. document · 7–10. teacher judgement

### Teacher Notes {: #teacher-notes }

**Why this order.** Listening before reading stops the student from "reading with the ears" — at A1 the habit of matching sound to text too early blocks real listening later. From Lesson 3 we can shorten the gap.

**What Lesson 1 deliberately does NOT do.** No past tense, no abstract vocabulary, no long sentences. The passage uses only present simple and about 120 distinct words, most of them in the first 500 most-frequent English words. The present simple in part 04 is shown as a pattern taken from the passage, not as a rule to memorise; it is the first turn of the grammar spiral, and Lesson 2 comes back to it.

**Success criteria for Lesson 1.** The student should be able to:

- answer the three listening questions correctly on the second hearing;
- read the passage aloud in under 2 minutes without stopping;
- use 8 of the 12 key words in their own sentence;
- write 6 correct simple sentences about their own morning.

**If it is too easy:** move to Lesson 2 with a 250-word passage, add past simple, and add a 2-question summary task.
**If it is too hard:** split the passage into two halves across two weeks and cut the vocabulary list to 8 words.

**Toward B2.** The TOEFL question types in Part A (factual, negative factual, vocabulary in context, reference, inference) are the same five types the student will meet at B2 level. We keep the types constant for 8 months and raise only the text difficulty — so the exam format never becomes the obstacle.
